title: Vendor Binary Integrity and Transit Verification Exhibit
content:
Purpose:
This exhibit defines the minimum contractual and operational requirements Redwood Inference requires from suppliers that deliver compiled binaries, container images, or other executable artifacts to Redwood-managed environments. The goal is to ensure cryptographic integrity, provable build provenance, tamper-resistant transit, and timely remediation and rollback capabilities in the event of supply-chain compromise.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to every third-party supplier and subprocessor that provides pre-built binaries, container images (OCI), VM images, runtime libraries, device firmware, or equivalent delivered artifacts that Redwood deploys or distributes to customer environments.
- Excludes pure source-only deliverables where Redwood performs compilation in a controlled build environment, except where supplier also provides prebuilt artifacts.

Defined terms (for exhibit use):
- "Artifact": any compiled binary, container/OCI image, firmware, or packaged executable delivered by Supplier.
- "SBOM": Software Bill of Materials in CycloneDX or SPDX format.
- "Attestation": cryptographically-signed provenance describing the build inputs, builder identity, CI job id, timestamps, and materials (as per SLSA 3+/Provenance).
- "Signature Verifier": Redwood or automated endpoint used by Redwood to verify artifact signatures and provenance.

Supplier obligations (minimum):
1) Signed Artifact Delivery
- All artifacts must be signed using a recognized code-signing mechanism (e.g., cosign/PKI, vendor-managed hardware key) with signatures bundled in artifact manifest or accompanied by detached signature files.
- Signatures must include timestamping (RFC 3161 or equivalent) to prevent trivial replay/reshaping attacks.

2) SBOM and Provenance
- Supplier must deliver an SBOM for each artifact in CycloneDX v1.4+ or SPDX v2.3+ format and a SLSA-aligned build provenance attestation that lists build inputs, exact source commit hashes, dependency versions, and CI job identifiers.
- SBOM and provenance must be bound to the artifact via cryptographic signature or manifest hash (sha256).

3) Reproducible Build Evidence (where feasible)
- For components where reproducible builds are practical, Supplier must provide documentation and minimal instructions to reproduce the build and an optional reproducible-build proof (binary equivalence or reproducible digest). Where reproducibility is infeasible, Supplier must explain constraints and provide compensating controls.

4) Transport and Transit Integrity
- All artifact transmissions to Redwood must use TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 preferred) with mutual TLS or signed manifests. When pushing images to registries, registry TLS and access controls must be enforced and documented.
- For large/air-gapped deliveries, Supplier must provide signed checksums (SHA256) and evidence of secure courier or out-of-band verification.

5) Continuous Verification Endpoint
- Supplier shall provide or expose an HTTPS endpoint (or registry manifest endpoint) that allows Redwood to programmatically fetch the latest signed provenance, SBOM, and signature bundles. The endpoint must support structured responses and return metadata for a minimum of 12 months.

6) Rotation, Revocation, and Key Management
- Supplier must maintain documented key management processes for signing keys (KMS/HSM usage recommended) and commit to immediate revocation and re-issuance of keys upon suspected compromise. The supplier must notify Redwood within 24 hours of any key compromise or suspected signing integrity failure.

7) Vulnerability & Patch / Rollback SLAs
- Supplier must provide a security contact and patching SLA for supply-chain vulnerabilities affecting delivered artifacts: initial triage within 48 hours, remediation plan within 5 business days, and production-ready patch or rollback instructions within 20 business days unless otherwise escalated.
- For critical vulnerabilities (CVSS 9.0+ or product-impacting supply-chain compromise), Supplier must make emergency rollback or mitigations available within 72 hours or provide compensating mitigations to Redwood.

8) Forensics and Evidence Preservation
- On request, Supplier must preserve and ship build logs, CI job logs, artifacts, and related metadata for forensic review for a minimum of 90 days. Longer preservation (1 year) must be offered for critical components on request with cost pass-through disclosed in advance.

Verification & Audit rights:
- Redwood reserves the right to perform supplier audits (remote or on-site) to verify signing practices, SBOM accuracy, and build provenance. The supplier must cooperate and provide requested artifacts, attestations, and access to build/process documentation within 10 business days of an audit notice.
- Redwood may run automated verification (signature validation, SBOM parsing, SLSA provenance checks) as part of continuous CI gating. Supplier agrees artifacts failing Redwood verification may be rejected from deployment until issue is resolved.

Contractual remedies and escalations:
- Material Failures: If supplier fails to comply with any material obligation in this exhibit (e.g., absent signatures, missing SBOMs for critical artifacts, refusal of audit), Redwood may suspend acceptance of further artifacts, require escrow/air-gap delivery, or terminate the affected workstream with 30 days' notice.
- Escalation Path: Security contact -> Supplier security manager -> Supplier CTO/legal -> Redwood security ops. Notification times in obligations above are binding for escalation.

Sample clause language (to incorporate into Master Services Agreement or DPA exhibits):
"Supplier shall deliver to Redwood, concurrently with each Artifact, a cryptographically signed Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) and a build provenance attestation. All Artifacts must be signed using Supplier-managed signing keys protected in an HSM or equivalent and include cryptographic timestamping. Supplier agrees to maintain build logs and reproducible build documentation and to promptly provide forensic artifacts on Redwood's written request. Non-compliant Artifacts may be rejected and Supplier will remediate at Supplier's expense. Supplier will notify Redwood within 24 hours of any suspected signing key compromise or supply-chain incident affecting delivered Artifacts."

Checklist for integration teams (operational):
- [ ] Confirm SBOM present (CycloneDX/SPDX) and syntactically valid.
- [ ] Verify artifact signature with provided public key / keyserver.
- [ ] Validate provenance matches expected repository and commit hash.
- [ ] Check signed timestamp for freshness.
- [ ] Run SBOM vulnerability scanner; flag critical findings.
- [ ] Confirm endpoint for continuous verification is reachable and returns signed manifests.
- [ ] Document remediation SLA and supplier emergency contact info.

Evidence artifacts Redwood should retain after verification:
- Signed SBOM file (CycloneDX/SPDX)
- Detached or embedded signature files and signing certificate details
- Provenance / attestation JSON (signed)
- Registry/manifest HTTP response and ETags
- Verification logs (signature validation, hash checks)

Limitations and notes:
- For legacy suppliers or closed-source embedded firmware where reproducible builds are impractical, Redwood may accept compensating controls (attested build environment, third-party notarization, or escrowed source) on a case-by-case basis.
- This exhibit does not replace other compliance obligations (e.g., export controls, cryptography export licensing).

Recommended technical references to include in contract annex (non-exhaustive):
- SLSA (https://slsa.dev)
- CycloneDX (https://cyclonedx.org) and SPDX (https://spdx.dev)
- cosign/signing and sigstore (https://sigstore.dev)
- RFC 3161 timestamping

Example acceptance test (automation):
- Given: Supplier publishes image my-org/component:1.2.3 with artifact and signature bundle at supplier endpoint.
- When: Redwood CI fetches artifact, verifies SBOM signature, validates SLSA provenance and verifies image digest.
- Then: Redwood CI marks artifact as "verified" and allows promotion to staging. Failure at any step causes automatic rejection and alert to security on-call.

Sign-off / next steps:
- Security: review exhibit and map to Redwood verification automation tasks (ownership: eng-sre).
- Legal: incorporate clause into Master Services Agreement template for vendors delivering artifacts.
- Supplier onboarding: require checklist and verification endpoint provided during vendor onboarding.

Prepared by: Maya Patel, security-and-compliance.
Notes: draft focused on operationally actionable controls; intends to standardize artifact acceptance criteria and reduce time-to-detection of supply-chain compromise.
